title: Hearing loss: hair-cell regeneration
bottleneck: Sensorineural hearing loss, affecting hundreds of millions, results from irreversible loss of cochlear hair cells, which mammals cannot regenerate; hearing aids amplify but do not restore natural hearing, and cochlear implants bypass rather than repair biology.
why_it_blocks: Hearing loss isolates people socially and accelerates cognitive decline; a biological cure would outperform any device.
current_state: Gene therapies restoring single-gene deafness are advancing: Otarmeni, a dual-AAV therapy for OTOF-related deafness, became the first of its kind FDA-approved, and hair-cell regeneration via supporting-cell reprogramming works in animals. Regenerating hair cells in adult humans remains unsolved. Supporting-cell reprogramming has regenerated hair cells in animal models, but translating this to adult humans faces delivery and safety hurdles. The dual-vector success of Otarmeni suggests gene therapy can reach the inner ear, opening the door to regenerative approaches.

sources.title: Otarmeni Approved by FDA as First Dual AAV Vector Gene Therapy for Rare Disease
